name: WeedVision-14: A Field-Scale Image Dataset for Multi-Species Weed Detection and Segmentation Task
description: WeedVision-14 is a multi-format labeled image dataset comprising 10,461 RGB images of 14 weed species commonly found in major cereal cropping systems of the Indo-Gangetic Plain, India. The images were collected at the experimental research field of ICAR-Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), New Delhi (28°38′N, 77°09′E), under natural field conditions during the cropping season, with variations in illumination, background, viewing angle, camera distance, and weed growth conditions. After field collection, the images were pre-processed and standardized to a uniform resolution of 512 × 512 pixels. The dataset covers major weed types, including narrow-leaf (grass) weeds (Bermuda Grass and Crowfoot Grass), sedge weed (Rice Sedge), and broadleaf weeds (Green Amaranth, Lamb's Quarters, Nettle-leaved Goosefoot, Benghal Dayflower, Field Bindweed, Lesser Swine Cress, Common Mallow, Burclover, Congress Grass, Stonebreaker, and Horse Purslane). The dataset supports core computer vision tasks, including weed classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation. The dataset was labeled under expert supervision, with bounding-box annotations and pixel-level segmentation masks generated to support weed detection and segmentation, respectively. The bounding-box annotations define the spatial extent of individual weed plants and are provided in YOLO, Pascal VOC, and COCO formats, while the segmentation masks represent the corresponding weed regions at the pixel level and are provided as binary and multiclass masks. The dataset contains 16,079 detection instances and 20,414 segmentation mask instances across all 14 weed classes. WeedVision-14 provides a standardized resource for developing and evaluating computer vision models for automated weed identification, detection, and segmentation.
